h: Fire, restoration and the castle's royal graves
p: In November 1992 a fire broke out in the castle and badly damaged part of the State Apartments, including St George's Hall. The restoration took around five years, and the rebuilt rooms combine traditional craftsmanship with new design. Walking through them today, it's hard to believe how much was lost, and the story gives a different angle on how the building keeps evolving rather than standing still.

St George's Chapel is the burial place of ten monarchs, including Henry VIII and Charles I. Queen Elizabeth II was laid to rest in the King George VI Memorial Chapel within St George's in 2022, alongside her parents, sister and Prince Philip, and many visitors come specifically to pay their respects. The chapel is closed to sightseers on Sundays, when it's used for worship, though anyone is welcome to attend services.

Look for which flag is flying above the Round Tower. The Royal Standard flies when the monarch is in residence, while the Union Flag flies when they're not. During the winter months, the Semi-State Rooms are often open as well, including some of the most richly decorated private apartments, so visiting out of season can bring a bonus.

Allow around three hours to do the castle justice. Afterwards, wander down Thames Street to the river, where boat trips run along this lovely stretch of the Thames in the warmer months. The Theatre Royal is a much-loved local venue for a show, and the leaning Market Cross House, known locally as the Crooked House, near the Guildhall, makes a fun photo stop.
